slots.title: Moody's pegs 2026 US growth at 2.3%
slots.body:
Moody's expects US full-year economic growth of 2.3% for 2026 — above what many had been assuming after recent data.

The rating agency points to higher interest rates (what borrowers pay on loans), elevated energy prices, and a normalization of the AI investment boom as factors that could slow growth in 2027 and 2028.

The 10-year US Treasury yield was at 5.1% in the latest curve snapshot (the rate the government pays on long-term debt, a benchmark for mortgages and corporate borrowing).

The 2-year yield sat at 4.8%, leaving the gap between 2-year and 10-year yields at 0.30 percentage points — the spread investors watch for recession signals.

Does a 2.3% growth year change how you read the next round of labor data?

slots.title: IEA sees 4% less oil demand by 2035
slots.body:
The IEA says energy-security steps tied to the Iran war could cut global oil demand by 4% by 2035.

That is a long-dated supply-and-demand story, not a single-day oil print — but it lands while crude markets are already moving.

Brent crude was at $92.22, up 0.3%.

The US oil fund proxy $USO closed at $136.11, down 2.9% on the session.

Gold futures were at $3,741.00, roughly flat at 0.0%.

slots.title: China Treasury holdings at 2008 low
slots.body:
Foreign investors trimmed US Treasury holdings in September, and China's position fell to a level last seen in 2008, according to Treasury data cited by Reuters.

That matters because overseas buyers help fund US deficits — fewer buyers can mean higher yields even without a Fed move.

The 10-year yield was 5.1% on the latest FMP curve print dated 2026-11-17.

The dollar proxy $UUP was at $29.62, up 0.3%.

$EURUSD was at 1.10, down 0.1%.

Are you tracking official custody data or just the yield curve day to day?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Nov. 19, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 561.25 points and closed down 1.1% at 50,198.17, trading between 50,029.35 and 50,637.70.
That was the heaviest index decline among the major U.S. benchmarks on the session.

The Nasdaq Composite finished up 0.4% at 24,429.88, with an intraday range of 24,225.30 to 24,538.78.
Gains in select large technology and chip names helped the growth-heavy index hold green while the Dow weakened.

The S&P 500 slipped 0.2% to 7,323.63 after touching a high of 7,367.68 and a low of 7,285.76.
The broad index stayed closer to flat than the Dow, reflecting the offset from Nasdaq strength.

The Russell 2000 rose 0.5% to 2,714.31.
Small caps outperformed the Dow and S&P on the day despite the large-cap split.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 3.5% to 24.56, down from 25.46 at the prior close, with a session range of 23.45 to 26.26.

Among megacap chips, $AMD rose 5.3% to $530.14 while $NVDA fell 2.9% to $150.96 on volume above 343 million shares.
$AVGO gained 3.6% to $354.05 and $TSM added 0.8% to $362.62.

Energy and financials weighed on parts of the tape.
$CVX closed down 4.0% at $205.87.
$JPM fell 1.8% to $324.11 and $BAC lost 1.1% to $48.91.
The Energy sector average was down about 1.1% on Nasdaq, and Financial Services was down about 0.6%.

Consumer Cyclical was the strongest sector in the injected sector snapshot, up about 1.3%.
$ROST rose 3.3% to $227.64, $WSM gained 4.0% to $260.09, and $GAP added 2.5% to $19.84.
Several of those names were on the Nov. 19 earnings calendar in the data, with consensus estimates listed but no reported actuals in the feed.

Utilities lagged among sectors, down about 0.8%.
Healthcare averaged down about 0.6%.
$LLY fell 2.3% to $1,382.54.
Technology as a sector was roughly flat, down about 0.1% on average.

$CRM declined 2.1% to $190.40.
$INTU, also scheduled to report, closed down 2.4% at $313.24.
$WMT edged 0.1% lower to $127.36 ahead of its report date in the calendar.
$MSFT ticked up 0.4% to $508.29 and $GOOG rose 0.6% to $279.20.

On the calendar for Nov. 19, U.S. jobless claims releases were scheduled at 8:30 ET, including initial claims with a 197K estimate and continuing claims with a 1,710K estimate in the injected calendar.
The dataset does not include released actual figures for those prints.

Gold futures were little changed, up 0.0% at $3,742.80.
$USO fell 2.9% to $136.11.
Brent crude was at $92.21, up 0.3%.
The Invesco U.S. dollar bull ETF ($UUP) rose 0.3% to $29.62.
Bitcoin traded at $63,216.24, up 0.4%.

Treasury yields in the Nov. 17 snapshot showed the 10-year at 5.1% and the 2s10s spread at 0.30.

slots.title: Warner Music Nov. 19 on $0.36 EPS view
slots.body:
$WMG is on the calendar for Thursday, Nov. 19.

Analysts’ EPS estimate is $0.36.

Revenue is expected at about $1.91B.

The report breaks out how recorded music and publishing are tracking — subscriptions, ad-supported streams, and licensing — without needing label jargon: it is how much money came in from songs and rights.

That session also brings high-impact labor data at 8:30 a.m.
ET: initial jobless claims (estimate 197K), continuing claims (estimate 1710K), and the four-week average (estimate 192K).

Those claims counts measure how many people are newly filing for unemployment and how many stay on benefits.
